name: Residual fusion with alpha over a frozen strong model (Tip-Adapter, CLIP-Adapter, ControlNet zero-convolution, ReZero) and learned multi-cue association over off-the-shelf cues (CAMELTrack 2025 with cue masking)
bibliography: (1) Tip-Adapter: Renrui Zhang, Zhang Wei, Rongyao Fang, Peng Gao, Kunchang Li, Jifeng Dai, Yu Qiao, Hongsheng Li. 'Tip-Adapter: Training-free Adaption of CLIP for Few-shot Classification'. ECCV 2022. arXiv:2207.09519 v1 (19 Jul 2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.09519 ; code https://github.com/gaopengcuhk/Tip-Adapter . An earlier preprint of the same method, 'Tip-Adapter: Training-free CLIP-Adapter for Better Vision-Language Modeling' (arXiv:2111.03930), is a duplicate of this work, not an independent confirmation [uncertain: the earlier preprint was not opened]. (2) CLIP-Adapter: Peng Gao, Shijie Geng, Renrui Zhang, Teli Ma, Rongyao Fang, Yongfeng Zhang, Hongsheng Li, Yu Qiao. 'CLIP-Adapter: Better Vision-Language Models with Feature Adapters'. International Journal of Computer Vision (Springer template; the IJCV reference is in the arXiv v2 text), arXiv:2110.04544 v2 (25 Mar 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.04544 ; code https://github.com/gaopengcuhk/CLIP-Adapter (not opened). DUPLICATE NOTE: Tip-Adapter and CLIP-Adapter come from the same group (Zhang R., Gao P., Fang R., Li H., Qiao Y.) and use the same 11-dataset few-shot CLIP protocol, so they are not independent confirmations of 'residual alpha helps'. (3) ControlNet: Lvmin Zhang, Anyi Rao, Maneesh Agrawala. 'Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models'. ICCV 2023. arXiv:2302.05543, https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.05543 ; code https://github.com/lllyasviel/ControlNet (not opened). (4) ReZero: Thomas Bachlechner, Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder, Huanru Henry Mao, Garrison W. Cottrell, Julian McAuley. 'ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth'. arXiv:2003.04887 v2 (25 Jun 2020), https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887 ; published at UAI 2021 [uncertain: venue from memory, not checked]; code https://github.com/majumderb/rezero (not opened). (5) CAMELTrack: Vladimir Somers, Baptiste Standaert, Victor Joos, Alexandre Alahi, Christophe De Vleeschouwer. 'CAMELTrack: Context-Aware Multi-cue ExpLoitation for Online Multi-Object Tracking'. arXiv:2505.01257 v1 (2 May 2025), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2505.01257, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01257 ; code https://github.com/TrackingLaboratory/CAMELTrack (Apache-2.0); checkpoints on Hugging Face trackinglaboratory/CAMELTrack. It is a preprint: the arXiv page and a web search show no conference acceptance [uncertain: it may have been accepted later]. Related prior work by the same group, 'Weak cues matter for online multi-object tracking' (AAAI, cited in CAMELTrack), is a different paper and was not examined.

inputs_state_output: Tip-Adapter: the strong base is frozen CLIP (visual encoder plus the text-classifier weights W_c, zero-shot logits f W_c^T). The added branch is a non-parametric cache: keys F_train (the CLIP features of the few-shot images) and values L_train (one-hot labels). No state. Fusion is at the logit level: logits = alpha * phi(f F_train^T) L_train + f W_c^T, with phi(x) = exp(-beta(1-x)) (Eq. 3-4). Output: class logits. CLIP-Adapter: frozen CLIP. The added branch is a 2-layer bottleneck MLP A_v on the image feature (hidden D/4), randomly initialised. Fusion is a convex residual in feature space: f* = alpha A_v(f) + (1-alpha) f (Eq. 6); the same form with beta applies to the text weights. ControlNet: the strong base is a locked Stable Diffusion U-Net. The added branch is a TRAINABLE COPY of the encoder blocks, initialised from the base weights, fed the extra condition c through a 1x1 zero convolution. It re-enters the base through a second zero convolution: y_c = F(x;Theta) + Z(F(x + Z(c;Theta_z1);Theta_c);Theta_z2) (Eq. 2). At step 0, y_c = y exactly. ReZero: inside every residual block, x_{i+1} = x_i + alpha_i F(x_i), with a scalar alpha_i initialised to 0 and learned; this is a generic depth/optimisation device, not a weak-over-strong fusion. CAMELTrack: off-the-shelf cues per detection are box+confidence (motion), BPBReID part-based appearance (5 parts + global, 128-d each) and RTMPose keypoints. Each cue has its own Temporal Encoder (TE). The TE is a 4-layer transformer over the last W=50 detections of a tracklet (age positional encoding, CLS token), with hidden 512 for appearance, 128 for keypoints and 64 for the box. Each TE projects to 1024. The cue tokens are SUMMED (merge_token_strat 'sum', utils/merge_token_strats.py). GAFFE is a 4-layer, 8-head transformer that applies self-attention across ALL detections and tracklets of the frame (inter-object context). Output: one embedding per object; normalised Euclidean / cosine similarity feeds a single-stage Hungarian match with a similarity threshold (sim_threshold 0.1 for DanceTrack/SportsMOT, 0.475 for MOT17). Ours: the strong base is frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign appearance of each real detection region, compared with the exemplar (snapped to a detection), the previous target and a bank (cosines plus 32 PCA products). The weak branch is FlyVis activity on a bounded grey crop: 68 regional features (34 output types incl. T4/T5 plus 6-neighbour means) and a temporal state over the exemplar and search frames. The fusion point is concatenation into one HistGradientBoosting identity classifier (stage 1), followed by the full-box transfer gate (stage 2). Mapping: CAMEL's GAFFE (inter-object attention) is the closest analogue of our neighbour-relative features. CAMEL's per-cue TE is analogous to the FlyVis temporal state over frames. Tip-Adapter, CLIP-Adapter and ControlNet are analogous to 'frozen MASA cosine logit + alpha x learned FlyVis correction', which we have not tried.
fusion_and_training: Tip-Adapter: training-free. alpha (residual ratio) and beta (sharpness) are found by grid search: utils.search_hp scans beta over 200 steps in [0.1, 7] and alpha over 20 steps in [0.1, 3] (configs/imagenet.yaml: search_scale [7,3], search_step [200,20], init_beta 1, init_alpha 1.17). In main.py the search runs on the val split. In main_imagenet.py the search runs on the TEST features, and in both scripts Tip-Adapter-F keeps the epoch with the best TEST accuracy (main.py lines ~113-127). The reported alpha/epoch choices are therefore optimistically selected. Tip-Adapter-F unfreezes only the cache keys F_train, initialised as nn.Linear weights = cache_keys.t(), trains them for 20 epochs with AdamW and cross-entropy on the fused logits, and keeps the values L_train and both CLIP encoders frozen. CLIP-Adapter: the adapter is initialised randomly. alpha is set by hand per dataset (best around 0.2 on generic data, 0.6-0.8 on fine-grained or shifted data). A learnable alpha, or an alpha predicted by a hypernetwork Q(f, W), is mentioned as an option (Sec. 3.3); learnable alpha/beta are used for the text-adapter variants. The residual is presented as protection against overfitting and against forgetting of the base. ControlNet: base locked. Zero convolutions (weight and bias = 0) guarantee that the output equals the base at the start ('harmful noise cannot influence', Sec. 3.1). The trainable copy starts from the pretrained weights, not from random. During training 50% of text prompts are replaced by empty strings, so the branch has to read the condition itself. This is the closest analogue of 'mask the strong cue so the weak branch must carry signal'. Training shows 'sudden convergence' in under 10K steps. ReZero: a scalar alpha=0 per block, learned jointly with everything; no protection beyond identity at init. CAMELTrack: the TEs are pretrained independently per cue, then trained jointly with GAFFE for 10 epochs (lr 1e-4, weight decay 1e-4; about 1 h on one consumer GPU; 42.6M parameters). Nothing is zero-initialised: the CLS tokens and the occluded token are zeros, but the projections use the default init. Cue dropout (train/transforms/tracklet.py DropoutFeatures) is applied per TRACK ID: drop_app with p=0.4, drop_bbox p=0.1, drop_kps p=0.1 (configs/modules/track/camel.yaml). If all three would be dropped, one is kept at random. The dropped cue's token is set to 0 (det_tokenizers.py: output[drop_*==1] = 0). The strong cue (appearance) is therefore dropped four times as often as the weak ones, an explicit anti-dominance device. However, the paper (App. E.3) states that cue dropout 'showed no measurable impact'. Other augmentations: SwapSporadic p_swap 0.2, DropoutSporadic p_drop 0.2 (Gaussian decay with age, sigma 50), SwapOccluded p_swap 0.5 at IoU >= 0.5, and Gaussian noise on embeddings and boxes. Parameters were chosen by grid search on each dataset's validation set, the same sets used for the Table 5 ablations.
labels_and_loss: Tip-Adapter / Tip-Adapter-F: class labels, cross-entropy on the fused logits (F.cross_entropy(tip_logits, target)), 16-shot. Fine-tuning the label values L_train drops accuracy to 60.90, and fine-tuning both keys and values collapses (Table 6), so the supervision carriers must stay frozen. CLIP-Adapter: the CLIP contrastive (softmax over class text embeddings, temperature tau) loss on few-shot labels. ControlNet: the standard diffusion noise-prediction loss with the condition; no identity labels. ReZero: task losses only (language modelling BPB, CIFAR-10 classification). CAMELTrack: identity labels from ground-truth track ids of precomputed detections. Training samples are built 'association-centric': one random frame's detections versus the earlier tracklets, repeated across different videos until P=32 detection-tracklet pairs. The loss is InfoNCE (pytorch_metric_learning NTXentLoss with cosine similarity and AvgNonZeroReducer, camel.py line 139), computed over all tracklets and detections in a sample. All other identities in the scene are negatives, so similar neighbours are negatives by construction. Hard negatives are created synthetically by identity swaps between overlapping tracklets (SwapOccluded, IoU >= 0.5, p=0.5), by sporadic swaps, and by dropout of recent detections (re-entry). No explicit class-imbalance weighting; the InfoNCE softmax over candidates handles the many-negatives imbalance. Transfer note: our stage-1 labels (is this region the target) with 928 positives among 5345 candidate rows on train26 (runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json identity.base) fit a within-query softmax/InfoNCE over the 18 candidate slots better than independent binary rows.
data_camera_resolution_rate: Tip-Adapter / CLIP-Adapter: 11 image classification datasets (ImageNet, Caltech101, OxfordPets, StanfordCars, Flowers102, Food101, FGVCAircraft, SUN397, DTD, EuroSAT, UCF101). 1/2/4/8/16 shots; tests on full test sets; ImageNet-V2 and ImageNet-Sketch for distribution shift; CLIP RN50 (Tip-Adapter Table 1) and other backbones. Static images, no video, no camera motion, no lighting stratification. ControlNet: about 25K-3M image-condition pairs per condition type (Canny, depth, pose, segmentation, etc.) [uncertain: per-condition sizes not re-checked], 512x512 images. ReZero: enwik8 (character LM), CIFAR-10. CAMELTrack: DanceTrack (dancers with near-identical appearance, erratic motion, heavy occlusion), SportsMOT (players with team jerseys, distant camera), MOT17 (pedestrians, 7 train/7 test videos), PoseTrack21 and BEE24 (bees; re-ID unusable, so motion/position only). Video counts from memory: DanceTrack 100 videos (40/25/35 train/val/test) and SportsMOT 240 videos [uncertain: not re-checked in this session]. The detector is a YOLOX taken from DiffMOT. Ablations are run on the DanceTrack and SportsMOT validation sets. No BDD100K, no explicit low light or glare subsets, no vehicles; the scenes are mostly people with a fixed or slowly moving camera, apart from sports broadcast panning.

distinguishing_ablations: Base alone vs base+branch: present in all sources as alpha=0 rows (Tip-Adapter Table 4, CLIP-Adapter Table 6) or as single-cue rows (CAMEL Exp2 vs Exp8). Base + NON-INFORMATIVE branch of equal capacity: ABSENT in every source. No shuffled-label cache, no random-feature adapter, no random cue token in CAMEL. The closest are Tip-Adapter's cache-size ablation (fewer prototypes, still informative) and CLIP-Adapter's bottleneck ablation (capacity, not information). The 'gain of a weak cue over a strong appearance base' therefore cannot be separated from 'gain from extra trainable capacity or extra training'. Clean weak-over-strong evidence: (a) CAMEL keypoints over appearance+box (Exp10 vs Exp8): +2.7 HOTA / +4.8 IDF1 on DanceTrack, where dancers look alike and occlude, but +0.1 HOTA / +0.6 IDF1 on SportsMOT (distant camera, noisy pose; the authors call it no improvement). A weak cue helps only where the base is weak AND the cue is measured reliably. (b) Box/motion over appearance: Exp2 vs Exp8 gives +10.0 HOTA on DanceTrack (appearance weak) and +2.6 on SportsMOT, but Exp8 also adds GAFFE, so the motion and fusion contributions are confounded; an 'App TE + GAFFE' row is not reported. (c) Static equal-weight fusion (Exp6) gives NO gain over the better single cue (DanceTrack 54.3 = KF alone; SportsMOT 75.8 < 76.0 EMA alone). Naive fixed-alpha addition of a weak cue can add exactly nothing, and a learned fusion (Exp7) recovers +2.2/+3.6. Exp7 also turns DA on, again confounded. (d) Cue dropout: App. E.3 says 'no measurable impact'; no table. Removing ALL augmentations (Exp9 vs Exp10) costs -4.1/-3.7 HOTA. Residual alpha: Tip-Adapter and CLIP-Adapter show an inverted U; too large alpha HURTS below the base (Tip alpha=4: 59.14 < 60.33; CLIP-Adapter ImageNet alpha=1: 59.05 < 60.46). The gain is largest where the base is weakest relative to the task (DTD +25.3 at alpha 0.6 vs ImageNet +0.87), and it nearly vanishes under distribution shift (Sketch +0.46). Zero-init: ReZero alpha=0 vs alpha=1 has the same final BPB (1.17), with only faster convergence. ControlNet without zero conv degrades, but only qualitatively (6 samples). No source reports seeds or confidence intervals. Tip-Adapter's alpha and epoch were partly selected on the test set (code).
explanations_addressed: (1) Fly features carry no unique identity information beyond appearance. CAUTION/indirect: none of the sources tests this. In Tip-Adapter the added branch carries NEW labelled information (few-shot labels the base never saw). ReZero shows that zero-init does not change the final capacity (BPB 1.17 both ways). A residual/alpha or zero-init design therefore cannot create information; it can only (a) prevent harm at start and (b) regularise. The alpha-sweep curve itself is a direct diagnostic: if the calibration-selected alpha is 0 or the curve is flat, there is no usable unique information for that projection family. (2) Information exists but fusion/training ignores it (modality imbalance). DESIGN ANALOGY: ControlNet's 50% prompt dropout and CAMEL's appearance dropout p=0.4 (vs 0.1 for weak cues) are exactly anti-dominance devices; CAMEL reports cue dropout has no measurable impact. For our CURRENT failure, imbalance is a weak explanation: gradient boosting on a concatenation is not joint SGD, and trees split on fly features whenever they reduce loss (fly alone reaches AUC 0.95). The explanation becomes relevant only for a future end-to-end fly branch. (3) Saved readout features lost the information; new activity or a fine-tuned core is needed. DESIGN ANALOGY: Tip-Adapter-F (fine-tuning only the keys, initialised from data) gives +3.48 over training-free Tip-Adapter. ControlNet's trainable copy initialised from the strong weights beats the lightweight scratch branch. Both support 'initialise the fly branch from the pretrained FlyVis ensemble and fine-tune a small part', not 'learn a random adapter'. Unfreezing the label carriers or everything collapses (Tip Table 6). (4) FlyVis lacks the lobula/LC object pathway: NOT ADDRESSED. (5) Motion helps only in subsets diluted by averaging. DIRECT DESIGN EVIDENCE: CAMEL keypoints +2.7 HOTA on DanceTrack vs +0.1 on SportsMOT. CAMEL App. F explicitly proposes per-tracklet weights because 'motion cues better discriminate between similarly-appearing targets' while appearance dominates for distinct ones. CLIP-Adapter's optimal alpha moves with the domain gap. Together these support a regime-dependent alpha (gated by MASA ambiguity) rather than one global alpha. (6) Ceiling too low (+2.8 pp perfect identity vs +2 pp threshold): NOT ADDRESSED directly. CAMEL's oracle pair (Exp11 fusion oracle vs Exp12 association oracle) is a methodological template for bounding fusion gain by an oracle-alpha experiment before building a learned fusion.
evidence_strength: Tip-Adapter (ECCV 2022, peer-reviewed, code verified, widely reused) and CLIP-Adapter (IJCV, same group, same protocol, so not independent): strong for 'alpha=0 recovers the base, the optimum is an inverted U, and too large alpha harms'; weak for our question, because there are no seeds or CIs, alpha and epochs were partly selected on test data in the official code, and there are no non-informative controls. ControlNet (ICCV 2023, code public, not opened): moderate for the zero-init safety principle; the zero-conv ablation is qualitative only. ReZero (preprint v2, UAI 2021 [uncertain]): strong but narrow; it concerns convergence speed, not information. CAMELTrack (preprint, code verified, single runs, ablation hyperparameters tuned on the same validation sets): moderate for 'a weak cue adds only where the base is weak and the cue reliable'; weak for cue masking (no measurable impact, no table). Overall for the decision on FlyVis: MODERATE as design guidance, WEAK as evidence that a weak branch adds over a strong base when the information is absent.
difference_from_tried: Tried: frozen MASA cosines + snapped exemplar + 32 PCA products as base features; FlyVis D/C/R1 saved features (238 F1 columns incl. neighbour-relative) CONCATENATED into one HistGradientBoosting (300 iterations, 31 leaves, min_samples_leaf 40) that fits base and fly jointly; tagged previous target, bank, T4/T5 consistency; core identity fine-tuning prepared but not run. The residual-alpha mechanism differs in four ways. (a) The appearance score is computed first and FROZEN as an offset logit s_A. The fly branch only learns a correction g(fly) with logit = s_A + alpha*g. This is stacking with offset; it can be emulated with logistic regression with an offset, or with LightGBM init_score. The trees in our concatenation can already learn this function, so on saved features the residual form adds no information and no representable function; it adds only shrinkage and lower variance. That matters, because the fly gain fell from +0.409 on reused fit104 to +0.107 [-0.176; +0.400] on train26 (runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json paired.base_D-base), which is consistent with overfitting/variance. (b) alpha is selected on calibration videos with alpha=0 included, so the 'no fly' answer is an explicit outcome. (c) The loss is within-query InfoNCE over the 18 candidate slots (CAMEL) instead of independent binary rows. (d) The design allows gradient into the FlyVis core with a zero-initialised output (ControlNet/ReZero), which the boosting route cannot. If (a)-(c) on saved features give nothing beyond the boosting result, there is no difference that saved features can show, and only (d) remains.
math_precheck: CPU only, saved features: runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/train26_features_{D,C,R1}.npz (8326 queries x 18 slots x 238 F1, ident labels) and the fit104 features of the v2 runs (runs/z13_hybrid_identity_v2_20261026 pipeline). Step 0 (offset): with the existing nested folds, compute out-of-fold appearance-only logits s_A per candidate from the base boosting. Step 1 (alpha curve = Tip-Adapter Table 4 / CLIP-Adapter Table 6 analogue): on training folds, fit a small projection g (ridge-penalised linear or a 1-hidden-layer MLP of fixed width) of the fly block, with s_A as a fixed offset, under a within-query softmax (conditional logit) loss. Sweep alpha in {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2} on calibration videos. Report per alpha the held-out within-query log-likelihood gain DeltaLL = mean over queries of [log p(true|s_A + alpha g) - log p(true|s_A)] (a conditional V-information estimate) and the top-1 identity accuracy, with a paired video bootstrap. Step 2 (equal-capacity controls, same g, same alpha grid): eye input R1, stock C, within-query permuted fly rows (keeps marginals, destroys alignment), Gaussian features of the same dimension, and a Kalman/velocity block of the same parameter count. Step 3 (complementarity/oracle): let E_A be the queries where the s_A top-1 is wrong. Compute (i) the fraction of E_A where the fly-only top-1 is right; (ii) the oracle-per-video alpha (CAMEL Exp11 analogue, chosen with labels) giving the identity accuracy upper bound; (iii) the exact utility bound obtained by feeding the oracle-alpha identity scores into the existing stage-2 gate offline. Do not use a linear rescaling for this. Rough scale: train26 perfect identity gives +2.836 pp over the bench and appearance alone +0.660 (report.json true_identity-baseline, base-baseline), so the room left for any identity addition is about +2.18 pp in total. Step 4 (regimes): repeat Steps 1-3 in strata defined without labels: MASA top-2 cosine margin < median (similar look), low-luminance crops, glare, crossing/occlusion by IoU between candidates. DECISION RULE (fix before running): STOP the residual/end-to-end fly line on saved features if ANY of the following holds. (1) The calibration-chosen alpha is 0 in more than 50% of video-bootstrap resamples, or DeltaLL at the chosen alpha has 95% CI including 0. (2) The fly DeltaLL is not above the R1, C, permuted and Kalman controls (paired CI of the difference including 0). (3) The oracle-per-video-alpha utility bound from Step 3(iii) is below +0.3 pp over appearance alone; under this condition even a perfect learned alpha could not reach a visible bench effect, and the remaining hope is only new activity or a new pathway, not fusion. PROCEED to GPU (core fine-tuning with a zero-init residual readout) only if (1)-(2) pass on fit104 OOF AND the Step 3(iii) bound is at least +0.3 pp. A further train26 evaluation would be a second use of a set that was registered as one-time, so a new confirmation set or explicit author permission is required.
cue_role_and_regime: Proposed role: per-candidate additive logit correction on top of the frozen MASA similarity: logit_k = s_A,k + alpha(r) * g(fly_k, fly_neighbours_k). alpha is either one scalar chosen on calibration videos, or a small gate alpha(r) of label-free regime descriptors r (MASA top-2 margin, luminance, glare, candidate overlap), following CAMEL App. F's per-tracklet weighting idea and CLIP-Adapter's domain-dependent optimum. Training-only regulariser: appearance dropout (replace s_A by a constant for a fraction of queries, p about 0.4 as in the CAMEL config, or 50% as in ControlNet's prompt dropout), so that g is forced to rank candidates by itself. At test time the appearance score is always present. Target regime: same class, similar look and close neighbours (small MASA margin), crossings and partial occlusion where the appearance crop is contaminated, and darkness/glare where the MASA embedding degrades. A gain outside these strata (for example, on well-separated targets) would indicate leakage or geometry, not identity. CAMEL shows that the weak cue helped only on DanceTrack-type ambiguity (+2.7) and not with distant noisy views (+0.1); BDD100K distant vehicles resemble the latter, which is a risk.
no_fly_equivalent_control: The same projection g and the same alpha grid (identical parameter count and training budget) on: (1) eye input R1 (pooled grey crop luminance per region, same 68-d layout); (2) stock FlyVis C (to separate modernised D from stock); (3) a Kalman/velocity block: predicted-box IoU, centre displacement normalised by size, velocity direction cosine with the track, scale-change ratio and their neighbour-relative versions, padded to the same input width or with the MLP width adjusted to equal parameters; (4) an equal-dimension within-query permutation of the fly features (non-informative but same marginals, the missing control in all five sources); (5) Gaussian random features of the same dimension. Three-way rule: base (alpha=0) / base + residual on control (3) / base + residual on FlyVis D. A FlyVis result requires D > (3) and D > R1 with a paired video-bootstrap CI above 0. If (3) = D, the gain belongs to the tracker motion model, not to FlyVis.
bio_node_mapping: The residual branch g sits at the FlyVis READOUT node: it reads the columnar output types (T4a-d/T5a-d and the other 26 output types) per region and pools them into one object-level score. Biologically this pooling resembles lobula columnar (LC/LPLC) neurons, which integrate T4/T5 and other medulla/lobula outputs over a retinotopic patch [uncertain: which LC types receive which FlyVis outputs was not checked in this item]. The FlyWire 783 connectome (local copy data/flywire/783 per project memory) could constrain the sign and sparsity of the projection weights from FlyVis outputs to an LC-like layer. Zero-init/alpha corresponds to no biological node; it is a training device. The recurrent FlyVis state, which would be fine-tuned under a ControlNet-style trainable copy, is an existing node (neuron dynamics/parameters).
novelty_overlap: Nearest prior claims: Tip-Adapter/CLIP-Adapter (residual alpha over frozen CLIP), ControlNet (zero-init trainable copy over a frozen generator), CAMELTrack (learned fusion of off-the-shelf cues with cue dropout). None uses a connectome-constrained motion model as the added branch, so ours differs only in the branch content (FlyVis readout/core). The fusion device itself is not new.
candidate_node_change: Node: the FlyVis readout (plus, at step 2, the core parameters). Change: replace 'saved fly features concatenated into boosting' with a residual readout head. A linear or bottleneck projection (CLIP-Adapter found the D/4 bottleneck best) of the 68 regional activities plus neighbour means produces a per-candidate logit correction. It is added to the frozen MASA logit with a ReZero-style learnable scalar alpha initialised at 0 (or alpha chosen on calibration videos), trained with within-query InfoNCE over candidates (CAMEL) and appearance dropout. Step 2 (GPU, only if the precheck passes): unfreeze the FlyVis core as a ControlNet-style trainable copy, initialised from ensemble flow/0000/000, with the head's output layer zero-initialised so that training starts exactly at the appearance base. Optional regime gate alpha(r). Why it addresses a FlyVis problem: the current readout pools fly activity through trees that also see appearance and are free to overfit fly noise (fit104 +0.409 vs train26 +0.107). A residual head guarantees no harm at alpha=0. It also creates the gradient path needed to fine-tune the core on identity, which saved features cannot do. Equal controls: appearance only (alpha=0); appearance + stock C; appearance + eye input R1; appearance + an equal-capacity no-fly branch (Kalman/velocity) and permuted-fly; all with the same head, alpha grid, folds and gate. Condition to proceed to GPU: the math_precheck decision rule (alpha*>0 with DeltaLL CI>0 on fit104 OOF; D above R1/C/Kalman/permuted; oracle-alpha utility bound at least +0.3 pp over appearance) plus a newly registered held-out confirmation set.
strongest_objection: Every source improves over the base either because the added branch carries NEW supervised information (Tip-Adapter's labelled cache, ControlNet's new condition image) or because the base is weak for the task (DTD, DanceTrack). Residual alpha and zero-init themselves change only optimisation safety and speed: ReZero has the same final BPB with alpha=0 and alpha=1, and CAMEL's static weighted fusion gave zero. Our measured situation is the opposite. The base is strong (MASA AUC 0.965 on train26), and FlyVis D is not better than eye input R1 (-0.042) or stock C (-0.095) on train26 (report.json paired.base_D-base_R1, base_D-base_C). That points to absent unique information, not to a fusion defect. A linear residual is strictly lower capacity than the boosting that already failed. The best that can be expected on saved features is lower variance, which, given the CI of the train26 contribution, is unlikely to cross +2 pp. In addition, none of the sources contains an equal-capacity non-informative control, and Tip-Adapter's alpha and epoch selection in the official code partly uses test data, so even their headline gains are optimistic.
cost_and_hardware: The CPU precheck (Steps 0-4 on saved npz; logistic/conditional-logit heads and boosting OOF on 8326x18x238 arrays, with bootstrap): about 1-3 CPU hours [uncertain: depends on the number of bootstrap resamples and refits per fold]. No GPU, no new FlyVis maps. A residual head on saved features is also CPU-only. GPU stage (only if the precheck passes): fine-tuning the FlyVis core (734 parameters, 721 columns) with a zero-init residual readout requires re-simulating crop sequences for every candidate in every training query. Memory fits one 12 GB GPU easily; the time is dominated by simulation, of the order of hours per epoch over fit104 [uncertain: not measured]. The prepared core fine-tuning script would need the residual head and InfoNCE loss added.
